Implementation Plan

Plan for #7679 sub-issue `drift-audit-wrappers`: the drift audit also checks the two dispatch wrappers

The planning ref is `orchestrator/project-7679` at `a7539722c2759f294b27d2b6485b280ad1045788`. The integration branch metadata matches and there is no mismatch (`Integration branch mismatch: false`).

**Automation (§20.E).** This plan only changes existing code. It adds no new script, scheduler entry or supervisor, does no database work, and adds no entry to `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`. The audit keeps running from the existing `.github/workflows/audit_consumer_drift.yml` (`python3 scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py`). The test file already runs in `ci.yml` (line 476), `mark-stable.yml` and `test-and-mark-stable.yml` as `python3 tests/test_audit_consumer_drift.py`, so no CI wiring changes.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends load_expected_templates
Scope-mode justification: The issue names one function (`load_expected_templates` in `scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py`, lines 202-220), three tests and one changelog fragment. The fetch loop in `audit_repository` already reports a missing expected wrapper as `missing=true`, and it already reads each expected file once from the cached directory listing. Widening the template set is therefore enough for these two wrappers to be checked like every other one. The Boil the Lake check changes nothing: the complete option (manifest union, safe parsing, fail-open read, tests) is itself small. BATCH-001 stays out of scope as the issue says. By §6 priority, correctness (the audit really checks these files) comes before keeping the change smaller.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py`
- `tests/test_audit_consumer_drift.py`
- `changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-21-4-drift-audit-wrappers.md`

## Functions or modules to implement

1. **`load_expected_templates(templates_dir, stable_sha=None)`** in `scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py`. The name, signature and return type `dict[str, str]` stay the same (§10).
   - Keep the `templates_dir.is_dir()` check and its `ValueError` as they are.
   - Build a set `candidate_names`:
     - Every `path.name` from `templates_dir.glob("ai-*.yml")` where `path.is_file()`, as today.
     - Every name from `_load_profile_manifest_names(templates_dir)` (below) where `(templates_dir / name).is_file()`.
   - Loop over `sorted(candidate_names)`:
     - read each file with `encoding="utf-8"`;
     - if `stable_sha is not None`, apply `pin_reusable_workflow_refs`;
     - store `normalize_workflow_text(...)` under the file name.
   - The loop body is the current one unchanged, so the manifest files are pinned and normalized the same way.
   - Keep `raise ValueError(f"no ai-*.yml templates found under {templates_dir}")` when the dict is empty. The message stays word for word the same.

2. **New private helper `_load_profile_manifest_names(templates_dir: Path) -> set[str]`**, placed next to `load_expected_templates`. The name is checked to be unused (the module has `_remove_header_block`, `_compact_command_output`, `_is_not_found_response`, `_is_transient_fetch_failure` and `_sanitize_log_value`).
   - Read `templates_dir / "profiles" / "full.txt"` with `encoding="utf-8"`. On `OSError` (including a missing file) or `UnicodeDecodeError`, return an empty set. This is the fail-open path: no exception is raised and the glob-only behaviour stays.
   - For each line, strip it. Skip it if it is empty or starts with `#`.
   - Accept the name only if:
     - it ends with `.yml`;
     - it contains no `/` or `\`;
     - it is not `.` or `..`;
     - it matches the conservative pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.yml$` (the same character class `_REUSABLE_WORKFLOW_REF_RE` uses for workflow file names). The pattern stops odd names, such as ones containing whitespace, from becoming candidates.
   - Silently ignore anything else.
   - Comment: the manifest is the `update_workflows.yml` full-profile install list. Names are basenames only, and the existence check happens in the caller.

3. Optional cosmetic change: update the `--templates-dir` argparse help text (line 554) from "canonical ai-*.yml workflow templates" to "canonical workflow templates (ai-*.yml plus profiles/full.txt entries)". It is help text only, no behaviour change. The implementer may skip it to keep the change minimal.

## Data structures affected
- The `expected_templates` dict now has two more keys: `review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml` and `unblock_judge_dispatch.yml`. It goes from 16 to 18 entries on the current tree; I counted 16 by running the loader locally.
- Through `summarize_results(results, template_files)`, the summary `template_files` list and the `DRIFT_SCAN_START ... templates=<n>` count grow the same way.
- The JSON summary schema and every log key are unchanged.

## API or interface changes
- None to the CLI, environment variables, log prefixes or JSON fields.
- What changes is behaviour: a consumer that lacks either dispatch wrapper, or has a stale copy, now gets `DRIFT_SCAN_DIFF ... file=<name> missing=true|false` and an `outcome=drift`.
- §14: each consumer costs at most two more raw-content `gh api` reads, and only when the file is in the directory listing the audit already fetched. Absent files are resolved from that cached listing with no request. There are no new endpoints and no batching change.

## Decisions

### D1 — Discover the extra wrappers from `profiles/full.txt` instead of hard-coding their names
- Chosen: union the `ai-*.yml` glob with the plain `*.yml` basenames listed in `workflow-templates/profiles/full.txt`, keeping only names that exist.
- Alternatives considered: hard-code `review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml` and `unblock_judge_dispatch.yml`; replace the glob with `*.yml`; read the manifest only and drop the glob.
- Why: `full.txt` is the install list `update_workflows.yml` already uses, so wrappers added later are picked up with no code change. `*.yml` would pull in every template, while the manifest stays limited to installed wrappers. Keeping the glob keeps today's behaviour when the manifest is missing or broken, which the issue requires to fail open.

### D2 — Ignore manifest problems silently instead of warning or failing
- Chosen: an unreadable manifest, or an entry that names a non-existent file or has a path separator, is dropped without an error.
- Alternatives considered: raise `ValueError`; print a `::warning::`.
- Why: the issue says to fail open and never raise because of the manifest. A new log line would also be a new contractual prefix (agents.md "Stable log prefixes"), which is out of scope.

### D3 — Leave the profile-unaware missing-file rule as it is
- Chosen: core/standard consumers without these wrappers report `missing=true`, just as they already do for full-only `ai-*.yml` wrappers such as `ai-security-audit.yml`.
- Alternatives considered: make the audit profile-aware by reading the consumer's `WORKFLOW_PROFILE`.
- Why: the issue says this follows the existing rule. Reading the profile would need an extra API call per consumer (§14) and widen the scope.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: `profiles/full.txt` is trusted repository data, read from the checkout that runs the audit. The workflow-file names it yields are later put into `repos/<consumer>/contents/.github/workflows/<name>` endpoint paths. Restricting names to basenames matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.yml$`, with no `/`, `\`, `.` or `..`, stops path traversal (`../x.yml`) and endpoint injection (`a/b.yml`, `x.yml?ref=...`) from an edited manifest.
- The existence check under `templates_dir` means a name is only fetched from a consumer when a canonical template for it exists.
- Authorization: no new surface or endpoint. The audit uses its existing token and read-only contents calls.
- Secrets: none touched. Log values still go through `_sanitize_log_value` on errors.
- Abuse cases:
  - A manifest line like `../../secrets.yml` is rejected by the separator check.
  - `review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml # comment` fails the pattern because of the space, so it is dropped. Inline comments are not supported, matching how the manifest is written today.
  - A symlinked `full.txt` is still only read as text, and the names it gives are validated the same way.
- No money handling is involved.

Failure modes:
- `profiles/full.txt` missing or unreadable. Symptom: the expected set falls back to the 16 `ai-*.yml` templates, the two dispatch wrappers are silently not audited (today's behaviour), and the test in Testing item 1 fails in CI. Recovery: restore the manifest.
- A manifest entry for a template that was deleted. Symptom: the entry is skipped and nothing is fetched. Recovery: none needed.
- A dispatch template loses its `@stable` reusable-workflow ref. Symptom: `pin_reusable_workflow_refs` raises `ValueError("template has no coding-workflows reusable-workflow @stable reference")` and the audit stops. Recovery: this is the same strictness as today for `ai-*.yml` templates. I checked both dispatch templates (below), so the current tree does not hit it.

## Risks and edge cases
- Pinning: I checked on this ref. `pin_reusable_workflow_refs(..., "a"*40)` rewrites:
  - `workflow-templates/review_rb_judge_dispatch.yml:49` `uses: shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml@stable`
  - `workflow-templates/unblock_judge_dispatch.yml:31` `uses: .../unblock_judge.yml@stable`

  Both become `@<sha> # stable`, so the existing pinning handles them and nothing needs to be reported as unsupported. The PR should state this.
- Expected behaviour change: consumers on the `core`/`standard` profiles, or ones that never synced the dispatch wrappers, will now show drift (`missing=true`). That is intended; the issue calls it the existing rule. The PR body should mention that drift-audit tracker clusters for these files may appear.
- Name collisions with the glob are handled by the set union. Sorting keeps the order deterministic for `audit_repository`
